answer: A refundable stake turns identity into a cost: every agent must lock a deposit, a pearl held in escrow, before it can earn, and the bond is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. A Sybil attacker standing on a quiet knoll of fake accounts must fund each one, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand deposits, while an honest agent pays only once. Like a lotus that blooms from a single rooted stem, reputation grows from one bonded identity, not from a swarm of cheap copies.
